title: Contraction and Fixed Points
intro: A quantum reservoir has the echo state property when the channels its inputs select squeeze any two initial states together. This page makes that precise with the trace distance, contraction coefficients and channel spectra, and shows how a conserved quantity breaks it.

blocks.text: Trace distance and why it is the right metric

The trace distance $D(\rho,\sigma) = \tfrac12\Vert\rho-\sigma\Vert_1 = \tfrac12\sum_i\vert\lambda_i(\rho-\sigma)\vert$ is the maximum over measurements of the difference in outcome probabilities: $D = \max_{0\le\Pi\le I}\operatorname{Tr}\Pi(\rho-\sigma)$. Helstrom's theorem makes it operational: given one copy of either state with equal priors, the best guess succeeds with probability $\tfrac12(1+D)$. It also bounds every readout: for any observable with $\Vert O\Vert\le1$, $\vert\operatorname{Tr}O\rho - \operatorname{Tr}O\sigma\vert\le 2D(\rho,\sigma)$. So if two runs of a reservoir end in states at trace distance $\epsilon$, no linear readout of bounded observables can tell them apart by more than $2\epsilon\Vert w\Vert_1$. For one qubit, $D = \tfrac12\vert\vec r-\vec s\vert$, half the Euclidean distance of the Bloch vectors.
Channels never increase distance
For every CPTP map, $D(\mathcal{E}\rho,\mathcal{E}\sigma)\le D(\rho,\sigma)$ (monotonicity, a data-processing inequality). Unitaries achieve equality. The contraction coefficient

blocks.caption: The worst-case factor by which one application of the channel shrinks trace distance.

blocks.text: measures how strongly a channel forgets. For a qubit channel $\vec r\mapsto T\vec r+\vec t$, differences of Bloch vectors map as $T(\vec r-\vec s)$, so $\eta$ is the largest singular value of $T$: depolarising gives $1-p$, amplitude damping $\sqrt{1-\gamma}$, dephasing 1 (populations are never forgotten: $Z$ eigenstates stay distinguishable), and a full reset $0$. Contraction coefficients multiply under composition, $\eta(\mathcal{E}_2\mathcal{E}_1)\le\eta(\mathcal{E}_2)\eta(\mathcal{E}_1)$, which is all the echo state property needs.
Fixed points and convergence for a fixed channel

Every channel has at least one fixed state $\mathcal{E}(\rho^*)=\rho^*$ (the state space is compact and convex). If $\eta<1$ the fixed point is unique and $D(\mathcal{E}^k\rho,\rho^*)\le\eta^k$ (Banach). More finely, write the channel as a $d^2\times d^2$ matrix (its superoperator). Its eigenvalues lie in the unit disc; the eigenvalue 1 belongs to the fixed point; other eigenvalues on the unit circle mean undamped oscillations or extra fixed points. If 1 is the only peripheral eigenvalue and it is simple, the channel is mixing (called primitive when, in addition, the fixed state has full rank), and the second-largest eigenvalue modulus $\vert\lambda_2\vert$ sets the asymptotic rate $D_k\sim\vert\lambda_2\vert^k$. The memory timescale in steps is about $1/(1-\vert\lambda_2\vert)$.

Conserved quantities are fixed points in disguise. If an observable $Q$ satisfies $\mathcal{E}^\dagger(Q)=Q$ for every input (the Heisenberg-picture channel leaves it alone), then $\operatorname{Tr}(Q\rho_k) = \operatorname{Tr}(Q\rho_0)$ for ever: the reservoir remembers that part of its initial state and the echo state property fails. Symmetries of the Hamiltonian that the input map also respects are the usual culprits.
The input-driven case: the echo state property

A reservoir applies a different channel at each step, $\rho_k = \mathcal{T}_{s_k}(\rho_{k-1})$. It has the echo state property if for every input sequence and every pair of initial states $D(\rho_k,\sigma_k)\to0$; then $\rho_k$ is, asymptotically, a function of the input history alone. A sufficient condition is uniform strict contraction over the input set (Chen and Nurdin state a condition of this type, as a uniform bound $1-\epsilon$ on the norm of every input channel restricted to traceless operators):

blocks.caption: Uniform contractivity gives the echo state property and fading memory, with memory decaying geometrically.

blocks.text: It is sufficient, not necessary. The Fujii–Nakajima step 'reset qubit 1, then evolve with $U$' has $\eta=1$ for a single step: two states that differ only on qubits $2,\ldots,n$ pass the reset untouched and $U$ preserves distance. Contraction appears only over several steps, as $U$ moves the difference onto qubit 1 where the next reset erases it. The right condition is then on products of $L$ consecutive channels, and whether such an $L$ exists depends on how well $U$ mixes. Martínez-Peña and Ortega rewrite finite-dimensional quantum reservoirs in Bloch-vector (Pauli or Gell-Mann) coordinates as classical state-affine systems and use this to give a necessary and sufficient condition for the echo state and fading memory properties under standard hypotheses.
Seeing it: two copies of one reservoir

The plot runs two copies of the same reservoir from different initial states ($\vert0\cdots0\rangle$ and $\vert1\cdots1\rangle$ in the quantum case), feeds both the same random inputs, and shows $\log_{10}$ of their trace distance. A straight downward line is geometric contraction; its slope is $\log_{10}$ of the effective contraction factor per step.

widget.title: Two copies, same inputs: do they converge?

blocks.text: With 3 qubits, $h=1$, $\Delta t=10$, the distance falls by about one decade in 40 steps (from 1 to about 0.09). With $h=0.1$ it falls faster, to about $10^{-2.6}$; with $h=10$ or $\Delta t=1$ it falls much more slowly (about $10^{-0.7}$ and $10^{-0.4}$ after 40 steps): a strong field or a short evolution moves little information onto the reset qubit per step. Even $h=0$ converges here (to about $10^{-0.9}$), because $\vert0\cdots0\rangle$ and $\vert1\cdots1\rangle$ have the same $\langle X_j\rangle=0$; the conserved quantities below only show for initial states that differ in them. For the classical network (where the plot shows the Euclidean distance of the two state vectors), a weight scale of 0.5 contracts by about 15 decades in 40 steps, 1.2 still contracts (the input drives the tanh units into saturation, where their gain is below 1), and 2 barely converges. The classical sufficient condition is on the largest singular value of the weight matrix, not on its spectral radius; spectral radius below 1 is the usual heuristic, as The Echo State Property (#/qrc/foundations/echo-state-property) explains.
A conserved quantity, made concrete

Take the spin reservoir $H=\sum_{i<j}J_{ij}X_iX_j + h\sum_iZ_i$ at $h=0$. Every term commutes with every $X_j$. The reset of qubit 1 leaves the reduced state of qubits $2,\ldots,n$ unchanged, so for $j\ge2$ it preserves $\langle X_j\rangle$ too. Hence $\langle X_2\rangle$, $\langle X_3\rangle$, $\langle X_2X_3\rangle$, and so on, are frozen for ever: start two copies with qubit 2 in $\vert+\rangle$ and $\vert-\rangle$ and they never converge. The script checks this, and computes the spectrum of the fixed-input channel.

Output: at $h=0$ the fixed-input channel ($s=0.3$) has four eigenvalues of modulus exactly 1 (one for each conserved $I$, $X_2$, $X_3$, $X_2X_3$; the next is 0.9975) and the two copies stay at trace distance 1 for all 60 steps. At $h=1$ the leading moduli are $1, 0.9804, 0.9804, 0.962$, and with the random inputs the distance falls to 0.755, 0.499 and 0.257 after 10, 30 and 60 steps. With $\vert\lambda_2\vert = 0.98$ the slowest mode has a timescale of order $1/(1-0.98)\approx 50$ steps: this reservoir forgets, but slowly, so it needs a long washout. (The input $s=0.5$ is a bad choice for this check: it writes $\vert+\rangle$, an eigenstate of $X_1$, and then all 16 modes of qubits 2 and 3 in the $X$ basis are undamped, not just the four conserved ones.)
What this means for design

items: Contraction is necessary for a usable reservoir, but too much contraction is also bad: if $\eta\approx0$ the state depends only on the last input and the reservoir has no memory beyond one step (a quantum extreme learning machine, see Quantum Extreme Learning Machines (#/qrc/models/quantum-extreme-learning-machines)).

The useful regime has a contraction timescale comparable to the memory the task needs. The parameters that set it are the reset or dissipation rate, the evolution time $\Delta t$, and how well $H$ spreads information (its integrability, field strength and disorder; see Dynamical Regimes (#/qrc/models/dynamical-regimes)).

Symmetries kill the echo state property. Before trusting a model, list the operators that commute with $H$ and survive the input map; any that the readout or the dynamics can reach is a memory of the initial state.

Noise on hardware adds contraction for free: global depolarising noise with probability $p$ per step guarantees $\eta\le1-p$. Chen, Nurdin and Yamamoto build a universal class of dissipative quantum reservoirs from operations native to noisy gate-based devices and run small ones on cloud superconducting hardware.

blocks.text: Worked problems

blocks.title: Steps to forget
blocks.text: Each input step of a reservoir is followed by depolarising noise with $p=0.1$, and the step itself is otherwise unitary. Bound the number of steps after which two arbitrary initial states are within trace distance $10^{-3}$.
solution: Unitaries have $\eta=1$; (global) depolarising has $\eta=1-p=0.9$; contraction coefficients multiply, so each step has $\eta\le0.9$.

blocks.title: Contraction coefficient of amplitude damping
blocks.text: Find $\eta$ for amplitude damping with $\gamma=0.3$, and the pair of states that achieves it.
solution: The Bloch map has $T=\mathrm{diag}(\sqrt{0.7},\sqrt{0.7},0.7)$; $\eta$ is its largest singular value, $\sqrt{0.7}=0.837$.
It is achieved by a difference along $x$ (or $y$): for example $\vert+\rangle$ and $\vert-\rangle$, at distance 1 before and $0.837$ after.
Differences along $z$ ($\vert0\rangle$ against $\vert1\rangle$) shrink faster, by 0.7.

blocks.title: Spot the conserved quantity
blocks.text: A two-qubit reservoir evolves with $H = J(X_1X_2+Y_1Y_2) + h(Z_1+Z_2)$ between inputs, and the input is written by a rotation $e^{-i\theta(s)Z_1/2}$ on qubit 1 (no reset). Does it have the echo state property?
solution: $X_1X_2+Y_1Y_2 = 2(\sigma^+_1\sigma^-_2 + \sigma^-_1\sigma^+_2)$ conserves the total excitation number, so $[H, Z_1+Z_2]=0$.
The input rotation is about $Z_1$, which also commutes with $Z_1+Z_2$.
Every step is unitary anyway, so $\eta=1$ and nothing is forgotten; in addition $\langle Z_1+Z_2\rangle$ is conserved exactly.
No: without a non-unitary element (reset, dissipation, measurement) there is no echo state property, and here there is also an explicit conserved quantity.
blocks.answer: No: the dynamics are unitary, and $Z_1+Z_2$ is conserved
